title: Viva Engage: sensitivity labels for communities (Microsoft Purview)
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft's Viva compliance overview does not support sensitivity labels in Engage, but that overview now explicitly confirms support. The documented controls and roadmap details are supported; two portal paths stop on the correct pages but need their remaining steps.

claims.claim: This briefing concerns roadmap item 491918, sensitivity label support in Engage.
claims.quote: "id": 491918, "title": "Microsoft Purview Compliance Portal: Information Protection - Sensitivity Label support in Engage"

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.

claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2025.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2025"

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents applying Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and associated policies to Viva Engage communities.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.claim: Engage can have a more permissive default than SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.claim: When admins configure a community default label, it automatically applies during creation of a new community.
claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Community admins can change a community's sensitivity label and consequent privacy setting.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community.

claims.claim: A label's External user access setting controls whether guests can be added to a community.

claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Engage feature documentation says PowerShell does not directly support applying sensitivity labels to Engage communities.
claims.quote: PowerShell cmdlets don't directly support sensitivity labels. Users can't directly specify sensitivity labels for Engage communities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The documented PowerShell workaround labels the connected SharePoint site, which updates the corresponding Engage community label.
claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Viva compliance overview still says sensitivity labels are not supported in Viva Engage.
claims.quote: The Viva Engage features eDiscovery, Data Retention, and sensitivity labels are supported by Microsoft Purview; data loss prevention isn't supported.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence with 'The Viva Engage sensitivity labels page and the Microsoft Viva compliance overview both document sensitivity label support in Viva Engage.' Keep the existing links to https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/engage/manage-engage-communities/community-sensitivity-labeling and https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/viva-compliance.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Engage as a public-first platform in many organizations.
claims.quote: Engage is a public-first platform in many organizations.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Labels are unavailable for selection in apps and services until published through a label policy.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Container label settings are visible but cannot be configured before sensitivity labels are enabled for containers.
claims.quote: Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them.

claims.claim: Enabling labels for containers is a one-time procedure, not a new enablement for each supported application.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure:

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: container labeling requires administrator enablement and configuration before users can apply community labels.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them.

claims.claim: No admin UI for the tenant EnableMIPLabels container-label enablement is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: enable sensitivity labels containers EnableMIPLabels admin center UI tenant. Read Entra groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and Purview sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites; enablement is PowerShell. Engage's disable-label UI is a different control.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params updates tenant container-label enablement.
claims.quote: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The update body sets EnableMIPLabels to True, and reading that setting shows whether container labeling is already enabled.
claims.quote: If the sensitivity label was enabled previously, you see EnableMIPLabels = True. In this case, you don't need to do anything.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Configuring sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 groups requires at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in the tenant.
claims.quote: To configure this feature, there must be at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronizes sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID with the Execute-AzureAdLabelSync cmdlet in the Security & Compliance PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: It can take up to 24 hours after synchronization for the label to be available to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Community container protection uses labels scoped to Groups & sites and the Privacy and External user access wizard settings.
claims.quote: Privacy and external user access settings to configure the Privacy and External users access settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels reaches the page for configuring label privacy and guest access.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy'. The same wizard also contains External user access. The route is documented across https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites, both already cited.

claims.claim: New-Label with Name, ContentType "Site, UnifiedGroup", SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled, SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy and SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers creates the label and its protection settings.
claims.quote: Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization.

claims.claim: New-Label accepts the combined ContentType value "Site, UnifiedGroup".
claims.quote:
The ContentType parameter specifies where the sensitivity label can be applied. Valid values are:
- File
- Email
- Site
- UnifiedGroup
- PurviewAssets
- Teamwork
- SchematizedData

Values can be combined, for example: "File, Email, PurviewAssets".

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled $true enables Site and Group Protection on the label.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter enables or disables the Site and Group Protection action for the label. Valid values are:
- $true: The Site and Group Protection action is enabled.

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy accepts Public or Private when Site and Group Protection is enabled.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy parameter specifies the privacy level for the labe. Valid values are:
- Public
- Private

This parameter is meaningful only when the SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter value is $true or $false.

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers takes a Boolean that enables or disables guest access.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers parameter enables or disables access to guest users. Valid values are:
- $true: Guest access is enabled.
- $false: Guest access is disabled.

claims.claim: New-Label is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell and creates labels rather than labeling communities.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies reaches the page for choosing labels in a publishing policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a sensitivity label policy containing the named labels.
claims.quote: New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management"

claims.claim: The printed New-LabelPolicy call selects labels, not recipients or a container default.
claims.quote: This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The label publishing policy UI selects the users and groups that receive labels and policy settings.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: The policy settings shown in the publishing wizard depend on the scopes of the selected labels.
claims.quote: The policy settings that you see match the scope of the labels that you selected.

claims.where: Scope, first paragraph; Governance controls: policy-dependent label choices
claims.claim: Users assigned a publishing policy containing a label can select that label for sites and groups.
claims.quote: The users who are assigned a sensitivity label policy that includes this label will be able to select it for sites and groups.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, first bullet
claims.claim: Microsoft's container guidance uses Public for organizational access and the Engage example chooses a Public-privacy default.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, first bullet
claims.claim: Clearing a label's External user access setting affects new users but does not remove existing guests' access.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, second bullet
claims.claim: Label external sharing settings can let site owners set options otherwise restricted to administrators.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, second bullet
claims.claim: Label authentication context settings can also let site owners change settings otherwise restricted to administrators.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and policy propagation before troubleshooting recent changes.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against changing site and group settings after a label is applied, and advises waiting at least 24 hours if settings are changed.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites. If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, first bullet
claims.claim: The Entra group-label documentation differs by saying published label group-setting changes do not automatically apply to labeled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label in the Microsoft Purview portal, those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, first bullet
claims.claim: The Entra guidance requires manually applying necessary updates to affected groups.
claims.quote: If you must make a change, use a PowerShell script to manually apply updates to the affected groups. This method makes sure that all existing groups enforce the new setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, second bullet
claims.claim: Deleting a site-and-group label still included in label policies can cause creation failures for new teams, groups and sites.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Before deletion, Microsoft advises removing the label from every policy that includes it.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: After removing the label from policies, Microsoft advises waiting at least one hour.
claims.quote: Wait at least one hour.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: After that wait, Microsoft advises testing creation of a team, group or site and confirming the label is no longer visible.
claims.quote: After this wait period, try creating a team, group, or site and confirm that the label is no longer visible.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The label should be deleted only after confirming it is not visible in that creation test.
claims.quote: If the sensitivity label isn't visible, you can now safely delete the label.

claims.claim: Users need an appropriate subscription that includes sensitivity labeling.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage sensitivity labels page itself names no license.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage sensitivity labels license licensing. Read community-sensitivity-labeling in full and the Purview service description's sensitivity-labeling section; the Engage feature page has no licensing text.

claims.claim: Creating and configuring sensitivity labels and their policies requires Microsoft Purview portal permissions.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies.

claims.claim: The Compliance Data Administrator role group is an option for granting label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: The Compliance Administrator role group is an option for granting label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: The Security Administrator role group is an option for granting label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator can grant label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: The Purview label-management permissions are not required merely to apply labels in apps or services.
claims.quote: They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services. If additional permissions are needed for specific configurations that relate to sensitivity labels, those permissions will be listed in their respective documentation instructions.
